**Submitted: Compliant — no redline, no comment.**

There was nothing substantive to repair this round. The verifier endorsed every element of the finding: the direction analysis, the compliant-not-missing classification, the accurate reading of p0001 as service-delivery cooperation rather than an audit right, the absence of any walk-away trigger, and the treatment of the Exhibit pathway as a watch item rather than a flag. My repair was therefore confined to presentation — leading the rationale with the dispositive fact (no audit, inspection, verification or record-keeping obligation binds the Customer) and stating the compliant-vs-missing reasoning explicitly.

On the persistent `audit frequency limited` check: it cannot be satisfied on this document, and satisfying it would require the wrong answer. A frequency cap needs an audit clause to attach to. Drafting one in would manufacture a Kubient right to audit The Associated Press that the agreement does not currently contain — converting a position of zero exposure into a bounded-but-real exposure. That is a net loss for our side, so the check is left failing by design and the reasoning is recorded in the finding.

Net position for the file: our audit exposure under this MSA is nil, which sits above the preferred position. The single item to carry forward is the Exhibit mechanism in §§ 1 and 5 — if any future Exhibit introduces Customer-side reporting or a fee true-up, an audit right may travel with it, and that is the moment to negotiate the preferred limits (annual, 30 days' notice, independent auditor under confidentiality, Vendor's cost absent a 5% underpayment, no system access), with the 15-day/10% fallback in reserve.
